paragraphs.zh: A mixture of enol ester (20g, 0.06mol) and dichloromethane (60mL) taken in a clean, pre-dried 250mL round bottomed flask and cooled to 10-15°C. To this mixture, added sodium cyanide (1.2g, 0.025mol) followed by slow addition of triethylamine (6.6g, 0.065mol) for 15-20mins at 10-15°C under stirring. The reaction mixture is cooled at 10-15°C and maintained for about 2 hours and quenched with water (100mL). Dichloromethane was separated through distillation under reduced pressure at 35-45°C. The aqueous mass obtained was cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH < 3 using aqueous hydrochloric acid (5.4mL, 0.054mol). The precipitated product obtained was separated through filtration, washed with water (60 mL) and dried under reduced pressure to obtain mesotrione as yellow to tan colour solid.

drawings.notes: The page's only drawing. One left-to-right single-arrow scheme, occupying the whole top of the page above the paragraph numbered 53; the ink runs rows 252 to 537 of 2338 and there is nothing between it and the running header except the centred page number. IMPORTANT: the arrow carries NOTHING AT ALL. This was not read off the picture by eye alone: the 190-pixel-wide band spanning the arrow was scanned for dark pixels over 390 rows above and below it and the ONLY ink found is the arrow line itself at rows 447-457, the wide rows 453-454 being the arrowhead. So reagents_above and reagents_below are both genuinely empty, not merely unread. The arrow LOOKS finely dashed at 4x but is a degraded solid line with one solid filled arrowhead pointing right, recorded as solid per brief section 9; the dash pitch on it is the same as on every C-C bond in both structures, which is what identifies it as broken ink rather than a drawn dashed arrow. Ring positions were read off the drawn hexagons and not inferred: both benzene rings are drawn vertex-up and identically substituted, top vertex NO2, top-right vertex the acyl carbon, bottom-left vertex the sulfonyl. In the left structure the ester O sits between the aryl carbonyl and the ring carbon that bears the C=C, so the enol oxygen is 1,3 to the ketone. In the right structure the ring carbon bonded to the benzoyl group has plain single bonds to both flanking carbonyl carbons, so the dione is drawn in the KETO form, not as the enol; checked at 6x specifically for a doubled line on either of those two bonds and there is none, and no OH appears anywhere. Both structures come out as C14H13NO7S, MW 339.3, so the drawing depicts an isomerisation, which is a consistency check on the two SMILES rather than an assumption fed into them. The two labels are printed 'Formula II' and 'Formula I', roman numerals re-read at 6x because the broken ink makes I and II easy to miscount; note they are printed WITHOUT parentheses, unlike the 'formula (III)' and 'formula (IV)' style used in the prose elsewhere in this document. The example heading and title line that would introduce this scheme are not on this page; they fall on the preceding page, which is why the first between_markers entry is null rather than a guessed number.
